To find the area of a trapezoid, you can use the formula:

\[ \text{Area} = \frac{(b_1 + b_2) \times h}{2} \]

where \( b_1 \) and \( b_2 \) are the lengths of the two parallel sides (bases), and \( h \) is the height.

Given:
- Base 1 (\( b_1 \)) = 13 cm
- Base 2 (\( b_2 \)) = 16 cm
- Height (\( h \)) = 12 cm

Plugging these values into the formula:

\[ \text{Area} = \frac{(13 + 16) \times 12}{2} \]
\[ \text{Area} = \frac{29 \times 12}{2} \]
\[ \text{Area} = \frac{348}{2} \]
\[ \text{Area} = 174 \text{ cm}^2 \]

So, the area of the trapezoid is 174 square centimeters.
